cases.title: Inlay Pathar: Adivasi farmland taken for a Hyatt hotel at Kaziranga
cases.place: Inlay Pathar, near Kohora, Golaghat district, Assam, India
cases.point: Kohora, the village at the main gate of Kaziranga National Park in Bokakhat subdivision; the Inlay Pathar fields taken for the hotel lie on its edge.

lenders.name: Hyatt Hotels Corporation (through Two Seas Holdings)
lenders.role: Two Seas Holdings, an affiliate of Hyatt, held 50% of Juniper Hotels Limited, the Indian company that runs hotels under the Hyatt brand (Zee Business, 2023). Down To Earth reports Hyatt signed a memorandum of understanding with the Assam government on 23 September 2023; the state's communique gave an investment of Rs 100 crore for about 120 rooms on a 30-acre site.

cases.conditions: The state supplies the land. A notice from the Bokakhat circle officer dated 31 May 2024 told the farmer Lokhu Gowala that the land belonged to the Assam Tourism Development Corporation; the circle officer said it had been converted to patta land after being handed to the corporation in 2022, and that the farmers' use of it was illegal (Down To Earth). Farmers say revenue collection on their plots stopped around 2022 and boundary pillars went up in late 2023. No loan or lender condition was found.

companies.name: Hyatt Hotels Corporation
companies.role: Brand owner, part-owner of the developer through Two Seas Holdings, and signatory of the September 2023 memorandum with the Assam government
companies.desc: United States hotel group. When Juniper Hotels filed for its Indian listing in 2023, Hyatt's affiliate Two Seas Holdings held 50% of the company, which ran seven hotels and serviced apartment blocks with 1,836 rooms under the Hyatt brand (Zee Business, 2023).

companies.name: Juniper Hotels Limited
companies.role: Developer of the hotel in partnership with the Assam Tourism Development Corporation, according to the complaint
companies.desc: Indian hotel company owned 50% by Hyatt's affiliate Two Seas Holdings, 44.68% by Saraf Hotels and 5.32% by Juniper Investments (Zee Business, 2023).

cases.community: Down To Earth reported in 2024 that the Assam government treats about 60 farmers on the site as illegal encroachers, while the land rights activist Pranab Doley counts 45-odd families who have farmed there for generations; the farmers say they have worked more than 30 acres between them. Lokhu Gowala farms about six bighas, roughly 1.9 acres, of paddy; Minali Gowala about seven bighas; Jogeshwar Gowala expects to lose about three. On 7 June 2024 the Golaghat district administration tore down Lokhu Gowala's house. He had been summoned to a hearing on the land and was told the circle officer was unavailable. The Quint put the site at about 60 bighas, roughly 37 acres, of farmland.
cases.suppression: Assam police arrested Pranab Doley and at least four other people in July 2026. About 30 people began an indefinite strike on 13 July 2026 demanding their release, and the community called the charges unfounded (The Quint). The Wire reported on 30 July 2026 that Doley was in judicial custody. Neither report states the charges.
cases.outcome: The United States contact point received the complaint on 30 March 2026 and has published no assessment; its confidentiality rules keep the complaint text closed (OECD Watch). A committee appointed by India's Supreme Court found in 2018 that more than 22 structures stood on the animal corridors linking Kaziranga with the Karbi Anglong hills, and in April 2019 the Supreme Court banned construction of any kind on private land forming part of those corridors (Down To Earth). The hotel was still under construction and the families still resisting acquisition in July 2026 (The Quint; The Wire).

cases.confidence_note: Two national Indian outlets record the harm outside the complaint: Down To Earth the demolition of 7 June 2024 and the families' holdings, The Quint and The Wire the July 2026 arrests. The complaint text itself is confidential. Down To Earth names Hyatt's September 2023 memorandum with the state and says Hyatt has not officially announced the project; it does not mention Juniper Hotels, while the complaint names Juniper as developer and Hyatt as brander, operator and investor. A separate Taj resort is planned on eight hectares of the nearby Hathikhuli tea estate, so the two projects should not be confused. No response from Hyatt or Juniper was found.
cases.ecosystem: The site lies on the fringe of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage site, about 2 km from the park by The Quint's account, and the complainants place it in an elephant corridor and less than 1 km from the park. The Supreme Court's committee counted more than 22 structures on the Kaziranga-Karbi Anglong corridors in 2018, and the court banned further construction on private corridor land in April 2019.

cases.whole: Nothing has opened. The figures for the project are the state's own: Rs 100 crore, about 120 rooms, swimming pools and parking on 30 acres, from the Assam government communique reported by Down To Earth, with no independent check found. The Quint reported in July 2026 that the hotel was still being built and that the people opposing it expect the families who farm the land to lose their living rather than gain work.

cases.title: Yavatmal cotton sprayers and Syngenta's Polo
cases.point: Yavatmal town in Vidarbha, where the government hospital took in the poisoned sprayers from the surrounding cotton villages.

lenders.name: Syngenta AG
lenders.role: Swiss maker of the insecticide Polo. Public Eye's investigation records exports of more than 126 tonnes of diafenthiuron from Switzerland in 2017, of which 75 tonnes went to India, 50 to South Africa and 1.5 to Colombia.

cases.conditions: A product sale, not a loan. Diafenthiuron, Polo's active ingredient, was banned in the European Union in 2002 and in Switzerland in 2009 and was still being exported to India in 2017 (Public Eye, 2018). Maharashtra banned it provisionally in June 2018; Down To Earth reports the ban held for two months, and the national list of twelve pesticides to be banned in August 2018 left it out. No lender condition was found.

companies.name: Syngenta AG
companies.desc: Swiss agrochemical and seed company. Public Eye's 2018 investigation records it exporting over 126 tonnes of diafenthiuron in 2017, a substance banned for use in Switzerland since 2009.

companies.name: Syngenta India Ltd
companies.role: Sold Polo to small-scale farmers in India, according to the complaint
companies.desc: Syngenta's Indian arm, named in the complaint alongside the Swiss parent.

cases.community: Twenty-one farmers died of pesticide poisoning in Yavatmal district in 2017-18, the highest figure of any district in Maharashtra, and 63 died across fifteen districts; the Special Investigation Team's report counted 886 people hospitalised in Yavatmal (Down To Earth). Public Eye counted about 800 hospitalised over a twelve-week spraying season, several hundred of them temporarily blinded, and more than 50 men fatally poisoned across Vidarbha between July and October 2017. Police records list 96 of the poisoned as having used Polo, 60 with other pesticides and 36 with Polo alone (Down To Earth). The hospital in Yavatmal did not know what substances it was treating and had no means of testing for them; serious cases were given atropine (Public Eye). The complainants add that household incomes fell, that women took on care of sick husbands alongside field labour at lower wages than men, and that 28 of the 51 farmers in the complaint report lasting neurological and muscular problems.
cases.killed_note: Not counted here. Twenty-one farmers died of pesticide poisoning in Yavatmal district in 2017-18 (Down To Earth). Public Eye records Bandu Sonule, declared dead at 1.35 p.m. on 23 September 2017 at the Yavatmal government hospital after spraying Polo mixed with other products, with an autopsy finding death consistent with poisoning; Down To Earth records Shankar Nago Agalave, who sprayed Polo on 24 September 2017 and died five days later in a Nagpur hospital. The state investigation team's report names monocrotophos and not Polo, Syngenta denies that Polo caused the poisonings, and the Basel civil court has not ruled, so no death is attributed to the company.
cases.outcome: The Maharashtra chief minister set up a seven-person special investigation team in early October 2017. It found cotton plants up to 1.8 metres tall, worse insect attacks, spraying at head height which increased the share of pesticide inhaled, mixing of insecticides with plant growth regulators, no proper protective equipment, and a Polo leaflet it found illegible; it recommended the agriculture department supply protective equipment through the state farm service centres, which Down To Earth reported in 2023 farmers still lacked. In October 2017 the state agriculture minister announced an investigation into Syngenta over Polo; Public Eye says it is not known whether that investigation took place. The Swiss contact point accepted the complaint on 15 December 2020 and its final statement of 16 June 2022 closed the question of whether Polo poisoned the 51 farmers, on the ground that discussing it would prejudice Syngenta in the Basel proceedings; it recommended Syngenta review its complaints process in India, and its follow-up of 15 June 2023 said Syngenta had made that process more accessible while the complainants said the mediation brought no compensation and no change to Syngenta's distribution (OECD Watch). Three families, two widows and a surviving farmer, sued Syngenta in the Basel civil court in June 2021 under Swiss product liability law; the court granted them legal aid in June 2022 and, as reported on 30 June 2025, moved to taking evidence on the victims' use of Polo (Public Eye).

cases.confidence_note: The poisonings are recorded outside the complaint: the state Special Investigation Team counted 886 people hospitalised in Yavatmal and Down To Earth, a national Indian magazine, reports 21 deaths in the district in 2017-18 and police records naming 96 poisoned people who had used Polo, 36 of them Polo alone. The link to Polo is disputed. The investigation team's report names monocrotophos and does not mention Polo. Syngenta denies the health claims, said in October 2017 that there 'may have been other reasons' and pointed to plant height and farmer practice (Public Eye), and said after the mediation that it regretted there was 'no meaningful dialogue' (SWI swissinfo.ch). The Basel civil court has reached only the evidence stage.
cx: Public Eye et al. vs. Syngenta
Syngenta pesticide poisons Indian agricultural  workers
cases.whole: Syngenta said in October 2017 that Polo had been used in India for fourteen years with no reported fatal incident; that is the company's own account and Public Eye records it alongside 75 tonnes of diafenthiuron shipped to India in 2017. Of the 51 farmers in the complaint, 43 were hospitalised, 44 reported temporary blindness and 16 were unconscious for between several hours and several days; most could not work for long periods and a few for up to a year. Those are the complainants' figures. Four years of mediation produced a revised company complaints process in India and no compensation. The Swiss export of a pesticide banned at home since 2009 continued.

cases.title: Clearing inside the Ayoreo Totobiegosode reserve and the leather trade
cases.place: Ayoreo Totobiegosode Natural and Cultural Patrimony, Alto Paraguay, Paraguay
cases.point: Chaidi, an Ayoreo Totobiegosode settlement inside the PNCAT reserve in Puerto Casado district, Alto Paraguay.

lenders.name: Conceria Pasubio (Gruppo Pasubio)
lenders.role: Earthsight calls it the largest European buyer of Paraguayan leather over the ten years to 2023, taking about 39% of the country's leather exports, and traced its imports to three Paraguayan exporters: Cencoprod, Lecom and Frigorifico Concepcion.

cases.conditions: A purchase, not a loan. Earthsight says Pasubio's step before December 2023 was to obtain a blanket assurance from a Paraguayan ministry that its supply chain complied with the law, from a ministry Earthsight says has no jurisdiction over the relevant laws. Pasubio's December 2023 statement makes future purchases conditional on a Paraguayan supplier showing no link, direct or indirect, to cattle ranches inside the reserve. The EU Deforestation Regulation was due to take effect at the end of 2024.

companies.name: Gruppo Pasubio (Conceria Pasubio)
companies.role: Italian tannery buying Paraguayan hides; agreed in December 2023 to drop Paraguayan suppliers that cannot show no link to ranches inside the reserve
companies.desc: Italian leather tannery that supplies vehicle interiors to BMW, Jaguar Land Rover, Volkswagen, Peugeot, Porsche and Citroen (Earthsight, 2023).

companies.name: Yaguarete Pora
companies.role: Took title to 78,000 hectares inside the reserve in 2002 and carried out the largest clearances there
companies.desc: Cattle ranching company Earthsight describes as Brazilian, fined by a Paraguayan administrative court in 2010 for concealing information about uncontacted groups.

companies.name: Caucasian SA
companies.role: Cleared about 2,100 hectares inside the reserve in 2018 and a further 663 hectares in October and November 2019
companies.desc: Brazilian-owned cattle ranch north of Yaguarete Pora's land inside the reserve; Earthsight recorded more than 200 fires on it in 2020.

companies.name: Cooperativa Chortitzer
companies.role: Bought a ranch on the opposite side of the reserve in April 2019, where about 520 hectares were cleared that summer
companies.desc: Paraguayan Mennonite cooperative and meatpacker whose slaughterhouse FrigoChorti supplies the tannery Cencoprod (Earthsight).

cases.community: The reserve is the land of the Ayoreo Totobiegosode, the only people in the Americas outside the Amazon with members still living in voluntary isolation. By the end of 2019 about 53,000 hectares inside it had been cleared and stocked with cattle, converted since 2005 (Earthsight). The complainants say the loss of the forest they depend on for food and medicine drives them out of it and into contact they have not chosen. In January and February 2021 uncontacted Totobiegosode were reported approaching their settled relatives (Mongabay).
cases.outcome: Paraguay's Comptroller General found in 2007-08 that Yaguarete Pora's clearing licence had been issued illegally and filed a criminal complaint; the environment ministry revoked the licence in November 2008, by which time more than 2,000 hectares had gone; an administrative court fined the company US$16,000 in 2010 for concealing information about uncontacted groups; the licence was reissued in late 2013 without new documentation; the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights granted precautionary measure 54-13 in February 2016 ordering deforestation on Totobiegosode land to stop; and INFONA suspended all land-use change plans for properties inside the reserve in February 2018 (Earthsight). Clearing continued after each step. The Italian contact point accepted Survival International's complaint on 6 December 2023; on 20 December 2023 both parties withdrew, saying they had reached their own agreement, and Pasubio announced it would halt commercial relations with any Paraguayan supplier unable to give guarantees about ranches inside the reserve; the complaint closed on 15 February 2024 (OECD Watch). Earthsight says the pledge covers only this reserve, not other Paraguayan or Brazilian sources, and does not say how suppliers will be monitored.

cases.confidence_note: The clearing inside the reserve and the steps taken against it are on the record of Paraguayan state bodies and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, reported by Earthsight with satellite data and by Mongabay. The trade link is Earthsight's own tracing of hides from the named ranches through three Paraguayan exporters to Pasubio. Earthsight records that none of the Paraguayan firms or the Italian tanneries answered before publication, and Mongabay reports Jaguar Land Rover saying Pasubio found no breach of national laws after an investigation. Pasubio's December 2023 statement commits it to exclude such suppliers without accepting that it bought from them. Pasubio is a buyer, not an owner or operator in Paraguay, and the hectare figures differ between Earthsight's reports: over 2,700 hectares for Caucasian SA across 2018-19 in the later summary against 2,100 plus 663 hectares in the detailed account.
cases.ecosystem: The dry forest of the Paraguayan Chaco inside the reserve, about 550,000 hectares recognised by Paraguay in 2001. Yaguarete Pora cut about 60 km of roads into it after taking title to 78,000 hectares in 2002; large-scale clearing for pasture began in 2004-05; it cleared more than 2,000 hectares under the 2007 licence, about 5,500 hectares in 2014-15, 2,000 in 2015 and 900 in 2017. Caucasian SA cleared about 2,100 hectares in 2018 and 663 more in October and November 2019, and about 520 hectares were cleared in the summer of 2019 at the ranch Chortitzer bought that April. Global Forest Watch data showed about 100 hectares of new clearings between 2020 and April 2021, some in dense forest, and Earthsight counted more than 200 fires on Caucasian land in 2020. Earthsight says 13 ranches held titles covering most of the reserve.

cases.whole: What the clearing produced was pasture: about 53,000 hectares inside the reserve under cattle by the end of 2019 (Earthsight). Paraguay's leather exports in January to April 2021 came to 9,424 tonnes, a third more than the same months of 2020, and two of the three exporters linked to hides from the reserve increased their sales to Italy after Earthsight's first report in September 2020. Pasubio took about 39% of Paraguay's leather exports and tanned the hides for car interiors sold to BMW and Jaguar Land Rover. No figure was found for any payment to the Ayoreo Totobiegosode, and the land titles over most of the reserve remained in the ranches' hands.

Fails test 1 on the map's own standing precedent, stated in BRIEF13, BRIEF17, CHECK13 and the handoff: a foreign company that was only a contractor, supplier or buyer does not pass the link test. Equinor, Total and TechnipFMC were the customers for a platform built at a Korean yard in Korea, and the Norwegian NCP found they did not cause or contribute to the accident, only that they were linked through the business relationship. The six deaths are heavily documented in the Korean court record but the foreign tie is a purchase.
